program.name: SPAR
program.roundStatusEvidence: Fall 2026 applications have closed. Spring 2027 applications open around December.
program.programDates: Sep 14 – Dec 14, 2026 (Fall 2026 research period); Demo Day Dec 19, 2026; optional continuation after Dec 14
program.locationNotes: FAQ: 'SPAR is fully virtual and our mentees join from all over the world. There's no country or residency requirement.' US-sanctions compliance may affect participants from sanctioned countries/regions. Some projects state a preferred meeting time zone/location. Occasional optional in-person meetups mentioned.
program.compensation: Unpaid volunteer program; approved project expenses (compute, API/LLM access) covered; Demo Day prizes ($7,000 total last year)
program.commitment: Part-time, 5–40 hours/week depending on project (typically 5–20), ~3-month research period
eligibilityNotes: Open to anyone 13 or older, including high school students; no degree requirement.
Under-18 applicants must say so in 'Anything else?'; a parent/guardian consent form may be required.
No country or residency requirement, but US sanctions laws may restrict participants from certain countries/regions.
US-based F-1/J-1 students advised to check with their international student office (SPAR is unpaid; letter available).
No previous research experience required; mentors often look for technical or policy-relevant background.

aiPolicy.summary: All free-response answers must be the applicant's own writing with no AI writing, rewriting, or polishing (including Grammarly-style tools and AI translation); AI may be used only to choose projects or for high-level feedback, with an accessibility exemption on request; answers are screened with an AI-writing detector (Pangram).
aiPolicy.quote: Every free-response answer must be written by you, without AI writing, rewriting, or polishing (including Grammarly-style tools and AI translation). Your answers are how mentors understand how you think, and we can and will reject applicants for AI-written answers.

stages.name: Mentee application
stages.description: Single form (forms.sparai.org/spar/mentee-app): basic info, career/education (resume required; GPA/transcript optional for students), four short free-response questions (2,000-char limit; 'three to five sentences' guidance), availability (time zone, 80% credible interval of weekly hours, commitments, location), ranked list of 1–50 projects, data-sharing consents, how-heard, 'Anything else?', and a no-AI attestation. Fall 2026 window: Jul 28 – Aug 18, 2026 (AoE).

stages.name: Project-specific selection questions
stages.description: Answered inside the application form, one answer per chosen project that has a selection question (answer box up to 20,000 characters). Questions and limits are set by each mentor and published on each project page; can ask for experiments, critiques, or work samples. Example captured: David Bau's Fall 2026 project.

stages.name: Mentor review, interviews and assessments
stages.description: Mentors review applications (alongside an AI-generated evaluation) and may request interviews, a short assessment/trial task, or references; some technical applicants get a CodeSignal skills assessment. Requests due by Aug 30, 2026 (AoE) at the latest.

stages.name: Reference nomination (subset of applicants)
stages.description: Some applicants are asked to name one or two references via a 'Name your references' form; referees then complete a SPAR reference form.

stages.name: Matching and decisions
stages.description: Mentors submit ranked shortlists, applicants rank projects; an algorithm matches using both sides' preferences and hours; SPAR staff finalize. Decisions released Sep 7, 2026.

program.notes: Deadline: Aug 18, 2026 end of day AoE → 2026-08-19T11:59Z (FAQ: 'you have until noon UTC the following day'). No late applications. Application-form wording was read from the closed form’s source code and is recorded as not verified. Form-level AI notice: 'Do not use AI assistance to write in this application. Every free-response answer needs to have been written by you, without AI writing, rewriting, or polishing (including Grammarly-like tools or AI translation). Using AI will substantially reduce your chances of getting accepted.' Only one example project's selection questions are captured; the 228 Fall 2026 projects each set their own. Every application gets an AI-generated evaluation (Claude) shown to mentors; people make all decisions (privacy policy). No published time estimate. Next round: Spring 2027 mentee applications open around December 2026 (home page and closed form). FAQ: 'SPAR runs twice a year. The spring round opens applications around December and the fall round around July.' Mentor applications open a few weeks before mentee applications.

questions.prompt: How many hours per week are you able to commit to SPAR? (80% credible interval)
questions.helpText: We're asking for an 80% credible interval. In other words, choose a range wide enough that you'd say there's an 80% chance your actual weekly hours will fall inside it if you're accepted. Your lower bound should be hours you could sustain even if something unexpected came up. Please answer thoughtfully and err on the side of lower numbers. Many mentees overcommit, and this harms their experience.

questions.prompt: Projects
questions.helpText:
Important: add projects in preference order, with your top-choice project first, your second-choice project next, etc. We'll use this to decide which projects to preferably pair you with, though you'll be able to adjust this before final pairings. The first spot is special: when applications close, the project you've placed first is shown to its mentor as your top choice during their review, so keep the project you most want first. The rest of your ordering is not shown to mentors.

As this is a highly competitive program, we encourage you to submit more than one project application, and recommend applying to at least 4. If a project has a selection question, answer it; mentors use these answers to decide who to take on. You can find a detailed list of the projects and their respective questions on the SPAR website. We recommend drafting your answers in another doc and pasting them into the form.

You can come back and add more projects until applications close. After you submit, your confirmation email will include a personal edit link, so there's no need to fill out a second application. The same link keeps working after applications close: through it you can adjust your order of preference and withdraw applications while selections are underway.
questions.notes: Wording taken from the closed form’s source code on forms.sparai.org. The closed form does not display it, so it is not verified as the live wording. Linked sub-form: add 1–50 projects in preference order; each entry = project + that project's selection-question answer (see spar-project-answer). Section intro (shown as help text). Section warning: "Reminder: you may not use AI assistance to write your answers."
